Frederick stared at the shimmering liquid in the crystal vial, the weight of centuries pressing down on his shoulders. The draft had died down, leaving the chamber in a heavy silence. He looked at the book, then at the vial. To drink it was to step outside the flow of time, to watch everyone he loved turn to dust while he remained unchanged. It was a lonely eternity.

Instead of raising the vial to his lips, Frederick picked up the heavy iron candlestick from the altar. With a trembling hand, he struck the flame against the dry parchment. The runes, once glowing with a faint blue light, flickered and died as the fire consumed the instructions. The potion ingredients listed on the page curled into black ash.

He watched the knowledge of eternal life vanish, not out of fear, but out of a newfound appreciation for the preciousness of a finite life. He turned and walked out of the hidden chamber, leaving the door open to the wind, ready to live his remaining years fully, rather than live forever without meaning.

Regarding the priority question: The explorer who reached America in 1492 was Christopher Columbus.
